thread:
nisha: Heads up — we’re seeing intermittent NXDOMAIN for the ECR interface endpoint in prod-west (vpce-0a1b2c3d). A few pods failing imagePullBackOff and a big NAT egress spike as some nodes fallback to NAT GW.

kai: saw the same. Cloudwatch shows increased NAT bytes around 09:12 and lots of 504s from the endpoint healthcheck. Any recent infra changes to endpoints or Route53 resolver rules?

maria: quick checks: can you paste a failing pod's nslookup output and the VPC endpoint describe? I suspect DNS/private-dns got toggled.

nisha: here's a quick nslookup from an affected node:

```
$ nslookup public.ecr.aws
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached

$ nslookup 012345678901.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
Server: 10.2.0.2
Address: 10.2.0.2#53

** server can't find 012345678901.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com: NXDOMAIN
```

samj: can you run `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0a1b2c3d --region us-west-2`? we need to confirm `PrivateDnsEnabled` and the subnet associations.

nisha: output (trimmed):

```
VpcEndpoints:
  - VpcEndpointId: vpce-0a1b2c3d
    ServiceName: com.amazonaws.us-west-2.ecr.dkr
    VpcId: vpc-0ffeed
    SubnetIds: [subnet-aaa, subnet-bbb]
    PrivateDnsEnabled: false
    NetworkInterfaceIds: [eni-11aa, eni-22bb]
```

maria: there it is — PrivateDnsEnabled is false. That explains NXDOMAIN for the service-specific names. We used to rely on the endpoint's private DNS so ecr.* resolves to the endpoint ENIs. Why was it toggled off? terraform drift maybe.

kai: that will also explain NAT fallback: kubelet/containerd can't resolve the registry host so image pulls try public ecr endpoint and go via NAT.

samj: quick mitigation: enable private DNS on that endpoint. Command (will cause a small control-plane change but no ENI replacement):

```
aws ec2 modify-vpc-endpoint --vpc-endpoint-id vpce-0a1b2c3d --private-dns-enabled --region us-west-2
```

maria: After enabling, also confirm VPC has `enableDnsHostnames` and `enableDnsSupport` true. If those are off, private DNS won't work for instances.

nisha: ran modify command at 09:21:23 UTC. AWS returned modifying state. Re-ran nslookup 09:23 and now:

```
$ nslookup 012345678901.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
Server: 10.2.0.2
Address: 10.2.0.2#53

Name: 012345678901.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
Address: 10.2.7.45
```

kai: nice. Starting to see image pulls succeed and NAT egress back to normal. Any reason this drift happened? PRs, automation?

samj: dug into terraform plan history — the endpoint resource was re-created by a separate automation that omitted the `private_dns_enabled` flag. Looks like our infra-onboarding script created the endpoint with minimal options.

maria: action items: 1) Add a tf plan check to ensure `private_dns_enabled` === true for aws_vpc_endpoint of type Interface for AWS services. 2) Add an alert that watches describe-vpc-endpoints PrivateDnsEnabled=false for managed endpoints. 3) run a one-off audit across prod accounts.

nisha: created GH issue #1789 with remediation + PR template change. Also kicked off one-off scan; found one other non-prod endpoint with same drift.

deploy-bot: Incident automation: `vpce-dns-drift-prod-west` alert cleared at 09:31:12 UTC.

infra-bot: Note — NAT GW billing spike alert has auto-acknowledged. Recommend verification of cost window in the billing dashboard.

samj: will add a quick runbook step: when ECR/EFS interface endpoints show NXDOMAIN -> check PrivateDnsEnabled first, then SG/route table.

maria: also a reminder — if private DNS has to remain off for some reason, add an inbound SG rule on the endpoint's SG to allow 443 from cluster CIDRs and create Route53 conditional forwarders as fallback.

nisha: marking resolved. thanks all :thumbsup:

kai: thanks. I'll follow up with the terraform fix and alert.

nisha: closing thread — last pod recovered at 09:29:47 UTC.
